[b]Argos Nuclear Advancements Organization report on Lavian construction plans[/b]

The Lavan government is currently undergoing plans to build a second nuclear fuel recycling plant, which will cement it as the nation that recycles the most used nuclear fuel in Erene. While most nations simply discard their used fuel, the ULRs unique position encourages it to recycle its used fuel and even import it from others. Many factors play into this, the main three of which are fuel acquisition, managing nuclear waste, and managing foreign reliance.

[u]Fuel Acquisition[/u]
The Lavian state, despite powering much of its society with nuclear power, they paradoxically have barely any uranium deposits. Relying on foreign imports, the Lavian government gets its from uranium [nation]united hydronia[/nation] and [nation]Nordiheim[/nation], choosing to refine the ore into uranium cake and the fuel internally. While it would be easier to rely on the nations large oil fields, the Lavian government sees the cost as an acceptable expenditure to maintain a cleaner environment and energy system. The use of nuclear fuel recycling not only decreases the amount of fuel needed to be imported, it also produces plutonium, allowing the nation to maintain its strategic weapons stockpile.

[u]Managing Nuclear Waste[/u]
The recycling of nuclear waste not only allows for more use of fuel, but also less nuclear waste per year. Only a small percentage of fuel during the recycling process is deemed as byproducts. These byproducts cant be used as nuclear fuel or have any other use, thus being waste. Instead of using its fuel once, Lavia recycles it and reuses it in normal as well as fast-nutron reactors, following government set guidelines on waste management and reduction. 

[u]Managing Foreign Reliance[/u]
While Lavia will almost always rely on foreign imports for uranium ore, recycling gives the ULR an extra buffer along with its strategic fuel reserves to any international issues that may interrupt the supply of ore needed for fuel. While both nations Lavia imports from are both close allies, precaution is always needed for international dealings. Not only managing foreign reliance, but decreasing it, is a large strategic need focused upon by th govenrment.
